newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - AWB cuts 96/97 ASW pool price by A$15.00/t.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - AWB cuts 96/97 ASW pool price by A$15.00/t.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) cut its estimated 1996/97 pool price for benchmark Australian Standard White (ASW) wheat by A$15.00 a tonne to A$175.00, it said in a statement.
The estimated pool price for all grades of wheat except durum had been cut by A$15.00 a tonne, AWB said.
Durum's estimated pool price had been increased by A$10.00 a tonne, it said.
The pool price reduction is at the upper end of market expectations. Traders and brokers have been tipping a pool price cut of between A$5.00 and A$10.00 a tonne for at least a week.
The cut brings the pool prices back closer into line with cash and futures prices.
Australian wheat farmers were more focussed on daily movements of the market than at any other time, Ron Storey, AWB general manager merchandising, said.
The pool took a much longer look at the market than the daily movement of the Sydney and Chicago futures markets, he said.

"It reflects the returns we're able to gather from all markets over the whole of the selling season and it is misleading to concentrate on a single market indicator and try to suggest that the pool return will automatically follow suit," he said.
Predicting returns over the life of a pool, up to 18 months, was "pretty tricky", Storey said. But the AWB believed figures announced were obtainable and realistic.
The new estimates bring prices for durum 1 pool to A$235.00 a tonne, durum 2 to A$220.00 and durum 3 to A$175.00.
Estimates were based on the present state of the international market and the AWB's estimate of the way the market would trade over the life of the pool, Storey said.
The pool price cut followed an increase in the AWB's estimate of the 1996/97 wheat crop to 21.0 million tonnes from 20.0 million tonnes, he said.
Storey also said the harvest payment for wheat delivered to the AWB's 1996/97 pools would stand at 80 percent of the A$190.00 estimate of ASW pool returns at October 21.
It remained AWB policy to maintain the harvest payment rate throughout the harvest.

"Some traders in the domestic market seem anxious to undermine grower confidence in that figure. (But) the AWB harvest payment rate has set a floor... and (to) buy wheat for cash you'll have to bid wheat away from the pool," he said.
Close to 90 percent of deliveries in Queensland and NSW in the current harvest had been to the pool, he said.
Storey also denied that there was a prospect of imminent pool closure.

"There is no denying that this is a difficult marketing year, but the near panic that has been evident in the domestic market in the past week has been fuelled by inaccurate and unnessary speculation," he said.
Grains Council of Australia president Jeff Arney described the pool price cut as "disastrous", with ASW pool prices down by 29 percent from A$245 a tonne in six months.
The next AWB pools price revision will be on November 18.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
